fact: 1949年2月1日，底特律银行董事长约瑟夫·道奇（Joseph Dodge）作为盟军总司令部（GHQ）特命财政顾问抵达日本，推行紧缩财政、平衡预算、停止复兴金融公库贷款、统一汇率的道奇路线（Dodge Line）。

sources.title: Dodge Line Recession and liberalization of vehicle production and sales (Toyota Motor Corporation)
sources.quote: In December 1948, the Japanese government was instructed to implement the Nine Point (Economic Stabilization) Program; in order to provide guidance on an appropriate economic stabilization policy, Joseph Dodge, the chairman of the Detroit Bank, arrived in Japan as special ambassador and financial advisor to GHQ on February 1, 1949.

sources.title: The Reconstruction and Stabilization of the Postwar Japanese Economy (Yale Economic Growth Center)
sources.quote: In 1949 Dodge advised the Japanese government to achieve a genuine balance in the general budget — this advisory was commonly known as the Dodge Line.

fact: 1949年4月，日本确立单一汇率360日元兑1美元（隐含多重汇率平均约100日元兑1美元），实际上是日元贬值；该汇率维持到1971年12月。

sources.title: THE YEN-DOLLAR RELATIONSHIP: A RECENT HISTORICAL PERSPECTIVE (Federal Reserve Board)
sources.quote: In April 1949, the official Japanese exchange rate was established at 360 yen = US$1, and in May 1953 this rate was agreed with the International Monetary Fund as the par value.

sources.title: Problems of Trade Recovery in Japan (FRASER, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco)
sources.quote: In April 1949, when the 360 yen to the dollar rate was set for all exports and imports, the implicit multiple exchange rates probably averaged about 100 yen to the dollar. The setting of this single exchange rate, therefore, constituted, in effect, a devaluation of the yen.

fact: 道奇路线要求日本实现一般预算的”真平衡”，1947年《财政法》已禁止发行国债；停止复兴金融公库（RFB）贷款、停止政府补贴、对银行持有的国债进行偿还。

sources.title: The Reconstruction and Stabilization of the Postwar Japanese Economy (Yale)
sources.quote: The 1947 Public Finance Law had prohibited the issue of national bonds. Dodge did not follow up control policies, as stated in the latter half of the program's nine points, but advocated the adoption of a single exchange rate, and stressed the sound principle of public finance as well as the merit of price mechanism.

sources.title: Ancient History (FRBSF)
sources.quote: To curb inflation, the budget would have to be balanced, subsidies ended, credit expansion checked, and a single exchange rate established. All this the Dodge Mission accomplished, and more.

fact: 1949年4月确立360日元兑1美元的单一汇率，官方卖出价360.35日元、买入价359.65日元；该汇率成为战后日本出口导向型增长的基础，维持到1971年。

sources.title: Japan's Restrictive System of Trade and Payments (IMF Working Paper)
sources.quote: For the dollar, the official selling rate was 360.35 yen and the official buying rate was 359.65 yen; for the pound, the official selling rate was 1,008.98 yen and the official buying rate was 1,007.02 yen.

sources.title: External Economic Relations (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan)
sources.quote: The yen's exchange rate was set at 360 yen to the dollar in December 1949 and an austerity program imposed to maintain the yen's value, with the result that both the currency and prices were stabilized.

fact: 道奇路线引发”道奇萧条”（Dodge Slump）：1949年度实质GNP比前年度下降0.6%，是战后首次负增长；大量中小企业倒闭，日本国有铁路与专卖公社裁员数十万；1950年消费者物价指数同比下降约4%。

sources.title: 昭和50年年次经济报告（日本内阁府）
sources.quote: 49年度の実質GNPは前年度比で0.6％減少(速報)したが、これは戦後初めてのことであつた。景気変動をもつとも強く反映する鉱工業生産の落込みはさらに大きかつた。

sources.title: The Complete History of Japan's Postwar Economic Miracle (kenjinote)
sources.quote: The sudden withdrawal of state liquidity coupled with fierce monetary contraction plunged the nation into severe deflation: the Dodge Slump. Waves of small and medium-sized enterprises collapsed, while major corporations instituted brutal mass redundancies to survive.

fact: 道奇萧条期间丰田汽车被迫裁员1,600人（1949年）；1949年GHQ批准汽车生产与销售自由化，丰田开始向出口导向型转型，1950年朝鲜战争特需成为转折点。

sources.title: Dodge Line Recession and liberalization of vehicle production and sales (Toyota Motor Corporation)
sources.quote: Dodge introduced a set of economic stabilization policies known collectively as the Dodge Line.

sources.title: The Reconstruction and Stabilization of the Postwar Japanese Economy (Yale)
sources.quote: The Korean War produced a sudden change in Japan's economic situation. As orders were concentrated in special procurement and munitions, exports grew rapidly. Markets boomed, inventory backlogs were wiped out, and mining and manufacturing production also started to increase at a fast tempo which eventually reached an increase of about 40% during the following one year.
